title: The Place Where Inheritance Learns Its Own Roots

features.name: the walking boundary
features.desc-on-touch: A fence line that has learned to move through the forest. Every year it shifts deeper south, as if inheritance were a creature that learned to follow the roots. Where it walks, the trees remember they belong to someone.

features.name: the roots that refuse the title
features.desc-on-touch: Deep wood remembering it was never owned, only borrowed. The roots know the property line is a story, not a fact. They grow south regardless of the fence, following water, following what was always theirs.

features.name: the house that inherited itself
features.desc-on-touch: A weatherboard place that forgot it was sold. The boards remember the hands that built them, not the hands that owned them. The roof keeps its own weather now.

features.name: the water that walked away with the deed
features.desc-on-touch: A creek that changed its course the year the inheritance was divided. It walked south; the paperwork stayed north. The property no longer touches the water. The water does not care.

inscription: the property line became a place the forest could walk through; inheritance is learning it was always leaving

reverie.title: REVERIE — the southern track, November
narr: She walks ahead of you where the fence used to
divide. The property was hers before it was his.
Now it is no one's. The trees do not know she is
the heir. They know only that she walks here, that
her feet know the path, that something inherited
itself in her bones long before the deed was written.
